classification.difficultyReason: Sketch trigonometric regions, distinguish area from signed integral, and use equal regions to simplify exact integration.

content.prompt: Draw a rough sketch of the area enclosed between each curve and the $x$-axis over the specified domain, and then find the exact value of the area. (Make use of symmetry wherever possible.)

answer.worked:
The regions above and below the $x$-axis have equal area.
$$\begin{align*}A&=2\int_0^{\pi/2}\cos x\,dx\\&=2[\sin x]_0^{\pi/2}\\&=2(1-0)\\&=2\text{ units}^2.\end{align*}$$

answer.worked:
There are four half-arches of equal area.
$$\begin{align*}A&=4\int_0^{\pi/4}\cos 2x\,dx\\&=4\left[\frac12\sin 2x\right]_0^{\pi/4}\\&=4\left(\frac12\right)\\&=2\text{ units}^2.\end{align*}$$

answer.worked:
The regions on either side of $x=\frac{\pi}{2}$ have equal area.
$$\begin{align*}A&=2\int_{\pi/3}^{\pi/2}\sin 2x\,dx\\&=2\left[-\frac12\cos 2x\right]_{\pi/3}^{\pi/2}\\&=2\left(\frac12-\frac14\right)\\&=\frac12\text{ unit}^2.\end{align*}$$
